title: Universal-counit normalized derived finite evaluation
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, $S_{W,n}=(P_n)_W$, $B_W=\varprojlim_n S_{W,n}$, projections $\pi_{W,n}:B_W\to S_{W,n}$ and quotient maps $q_{W,b,a}:S_{W,b}\to S_{W,a}$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], for $W=T,T'$ and positive indices. Use completed-coefficient module pullback $G=g^*$ and its strict-tower version $G^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and the fixed finite interfaces of [def-cbc-completed-reduction-finite-interfaces].

The projection-defined ring map $c_g:g^{-1}B_T\to B_{T'}$ equals the integral coefficient map of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners] and is an isomorphism. Consequently $G$ and $G^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ are exact.

Let $\mathcal R_T$ be the derived strict reduction functor, $V_g=Lg^*_{\mathrm{Tow}}$, $U_n=\operatorname{ev}_n V_g\mathcal R_T$, and $H_n(K)=Lg_n^*(K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{T,n})$. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms. For a cochain complex $P$ put $P_n=P\otimes_{B_T}S_{T,n}$, let $\epsilon^{\mathcal R}_P:\mathcal R_T(QP)\to Q\mathcal R_T^0P$ and $\epsilon^V$ be the universal left-derived counits, and define
$$u_{n,P}:U_n(QP)\to Q\bigl(\operatorname{ev}_nG^{\mathrm{Tow}}\mathcal R_T^0P\bigr)$$
by applying $V_g$ to $\epsilon^{\mathcal R}_P$, then its universal counit, then exact evaluation localization. This is a natural transformation on complexes with exactly these components. Put $v_{n,P}:H_n(QP)\to Q(g_n^*P_n)$ equal to the finite derived scalar-extension counit followed by exact finite pullback localization. Both $u_{n,P}$ and $v_{n,P}$ are invertible whenever $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]; no boundedness is imposed. Let $\delta_{n,P}:\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}Q(g_n^*P_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}g_n^*P_n)$ be exact restriction localization, and let $E_n$ be the ordinary isomorphism specified in [lem-weil-pbc-ordinary-finite-evaluation-transition].

There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$e_n:U_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}H_n$$
such that for every K-flat $P$,
$$Q(E_n(P))\,u_{n,P}=\delta_{n,P}\,\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}(v_{n,P})\,e_n(QP).$$
The ordinary isomorphism is applied termwise in this equation. This is the canonical finite evaluation completedReductionFiniteEvaluation and its specified representative normalization, for every derived input, including unbounded inputs that are not complete.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to the countable tower of finite rings $Q_n=P_n$. Its specified isomorphism $c:g^{-1}B_T\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{T'}$ satisfies $\pi_{T',n}c=c_{g,n}g^{-1}\pi_{T,n}$. These are exactly the components defining $c_g$ in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Two maps to the limit $B_{T'}$ with equal projections are equal, hence $c_g=c$. The integral coefficient map of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners] is this same specified map; for arbitrary $g$ one can use the cartesian square with both vertical arrows identities, which are proper, so that $g$ occurs among its arrows. Thus the asserted equality is equality of the specified maps, and $c_g$ is invertible.

source.place: Tags 098T (lemma-morphism-big-small) and 097N (lemma-ind-etale-implies), via the cited finite-ring-tower coefficient lemma; uniqueness of a limit map.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], inverse image with scalars $g^{-1}B_T$ is exact. Extension along the ring isomorphism $c_g$ just relabels scalars: the tensor map $x\otimes b\mapsto c_g^{-1}(b)x$ has inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Thus $G$ is naturally isomorphic to that exact inverse image followed by scalar relabelling, and is exact. Kernels and cokernels of strict towers are levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Applying $G$ to each level therefore proves exactness of $G^{\mathrm{Tow}}$; the same node gives exactness of evaluation. Finite pullback $g_n^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], since $P_n$ is a finite discrete ring. Restriction along $\pi_{T',n}$ is exact: it changes neither the underlying abelian sheaf nor kernels and cokernels.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] for the exact $G^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ and $g_n^*$ of Step 2. Their universal left-derived counits agree, under the unique universal-property comparison, with termwise localization; in particular they are invertible on every complex. Use its exact factorization also for evaluation and scalar restriction. This gives the exact evaluation factor and exactly the comparison $\delta_{n,P}$ in the statement. These comparisons are natural on the homotopy category and hence on complexes. No flatness of a tower obtained after reduction is required here: the tower pullback counit is invertible on every tower complex.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, and its left-derived dual; localization factorization and universal property.

proof.text:
For every complex $P$, put $R^0P=\mathcal R_T^0P$ and write $D\operatorname{ev}_n$ for exact derived evaluation. Define
$$u_{n,P}=\lambda^{\operatorname{ev}_n}_{G^{\mathrm{Tow}}R^0P}\circ D\operatorname{ev}_n\bigl(\epsilon^V_{R^0P}\circ V_g(\epsilon^{\mathcal R}_P)\bigr),$$
where $\lambda^{\operatorname{ev}_n}$ is the exact localization factor from Step 3. This has the required source and target. Whiskering $\epsilon^{\mathcal R}$ with $V_g$, composing with $\epsilon^V$, and then composing with $\lambda^{\operatorname{ev}_n}$ makes this a natural transformation. More explicitly, for a chain map $h:P\to P'$, the three naturality squares commute in succession, so their composite says $Q(\operatorname{ev}_nG^{\mathrm{Tow}}\mathcal R_T^0h)u_{n,P}=u_{n,P'}U_n(Qh)$. All these squares already exist on homotopy categories, so the displayed transformation also factors through chain homotopy. Its components are the specified universal-counit components, without a choice of comparison automorphism.

source.place: Definition Tag 05S9: universal left-derived counit; formal composition of the given counits and exact localization factor.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism $h:P\to P'$ between K-flat $B_T$-complexes, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1) says each $h\otimes1_{S_{T,n}}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction to $B_T$ leaves cohomology unchanged. By [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], cohomology of strict tower complexes is computed levelwise (use its levelwise kernels and cokernels), so $\mathcal R_T^0(h)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of strict tower complexes. The additive functor $\mathcal R_T^0$ preserves shifts and mapping cones termwise: a cone has the two summands $P'{}^i\oplus P^{i+1}$ with its signed differential, and tensor distributes over these summands and carries that differential to the same matrix. Thus its homotopy functor followed by tower localization is exact. K-flat representatives resolve every complex by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] with the class of ALL K-flat complexes and target $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{B_T}(T))$. Its counit is invertible at every K-flat $P$; by universal uniqueness the same holds for the specified $\epsilon^{\mathcal R}_P$. The remaining factors defining $u_{n,P}$ are invertible by Step 3, hence so is $u_{n,P}$. Neither flat terms nor boundedness of $P$ are needed.

source.place: Tags 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side) and 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); homology.tex Tag 02MZ; derived.tex Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), applied to the actual derived category of strict towers.

proof.text:
For finite scalar extension use [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] with $B_T\to S_{T,n}$. Its universal counit $a_{n,P}: (QP)\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{T,n}\to QP_n$ is natural on the homotopy category and invertible on every K-flat $P$. Indeed such a $P$ itself computes derived extension, using its identity as the K-flat resolution. Define
$$v_{n,P}=\lambda^{g_n^*}_{P_n}\circ Lg_n^*(a_{n,P}),$$
where $\lambda^{g_n^*}$ is the exact pullback localization from Step 3. This is the finite model map in the statement, natural by the two constituent naturality squares, and invertible on K-flat $P$. Put $J_n=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}H_n$ and
$$b_{n,P}=\delta_{n,P}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}(v_{n,P}).$$
Thus $b_n$ is a natural transformation $J_nQ\to Q(\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{T',n}}g_n^*P_n)$, also invertible on K-flat $P$.

source.place: Tags 06YT, 06YU and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), specialized to change of rings on one site; derived.tex Tag 06XN.

proof.text:
Apply the ordinary natural isomorphism $E_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ordinary-finite-evaluation-transition] termwise and localize. On the full subcategory of K-flat complexes define
$$a_P=b_{n,P}^{-1}\circ Q(E_n(P))\circ u_{n,P}:U_n(QP)\longrightarrow J_n(QP).$$
Its factors are invertible by Steps 5 and 6 and the cited ordinary comparison. For any chain map $h:P\to P'$ between K-flat complexes, substitute the naturality equations for $u_n$, $E_n$ and $b_n$ into this formula and cancel $b_{n,P'}$; the result is $J_n(Qh)a_P=a_{P'}U_n(Qh)$. These maps and equations depend only on the homotopy class of $h$, since all three natural transformations used above factor through the homotopy category.

source.place: Paragraph 2; termwise ordinary finite evaluation, with the universal-counit comparison written explicitly.

proof.text: Work in $C=K(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$, with $W$ the quasi-isomorphisms and $Q_h:C\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$. This $W$ has right calculus of fractions by [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated]. Every object admits a quasi-isomorphism $P\to X$ with $P$ K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Apply [lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class] with $A=U_nQ_h$, $B=J_nQ_h$ and the $a_P$ of Step 7. Its hypothesis that $A$ inverts $W$ holds because $Q_h$ does; its naturality hypothesis is exactly Step 7. It gives a natural transformation $A\to B$ extending $a_P$. Both $A$ and $B$ invert $W$, so the fully faithful precomposition statement in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends it to $e_n:U_n\to J_n$. On each K-flat $P$ its component is exactly $a_P$, whence multiplying by $b_{n,P}$ gives the required representative equation.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic), Tag 06XN; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YS; resolving-class descent and the fully faithful localization property of the cited nodes.

proof.text:
For any complex $X$ choose a K-flat quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to X$ as in Step 8. Naturality gives
$$e_n(QX)=J_n(Qs)\,a_P\,U_n(Qs)^{-1}.$$
All three factors are invertible, so every component is invertible and $e_n$ is a natural isomorphism. If $e'_n$ has the stated normalization, cancellation of $b_{n,P}$ forces $e'_n(QP)=a_P$ for all K-flat $P$. The same naturality equation with $s$ then forces $e'_n(QX)=e_n(QX)$ for all complexes $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], agreement on localized complexes implies equality of natural transformations, and hence of the natural isomorphisms. This proves uniqueness. The fixed interface [def-cbc-completed-reduction-finite-interfaces] names precisely the comparison with this ordinary map and these universal-counit components, so it is $\operatorname{completedReductionFiniteEvaluation}$. The replacements in Step 8 exist for arbitrary unbounded complexes; no step assumes derived completeness.
